sections.heading: 1. Purpose and Scope
sections.body: This policy establishes how {org_name} manages AI risk and assesses AI systems before deployment for {system_name} within {boundary}, aligned to Texas SB 1964 and to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (the TRAIGA safe-harbor standard). Aligned to the statutes; not legal advice.

sections.heading: 2. Pre-deployment Impact Assessment

questions.prompt: Who conducts and signs off the pre-deployment AI impact assessment?
What template or method is used for the impact assessment?

sections.body: Before an AI system is deployed, {assessment_owner} completes an impact assessment using {assessment_template} that documents: risks of unlawful harm; the system's limitations; the information-governance practices applied; and, for heightened-scrutiny systems, the known security risks and the transparency measures in place. The assessment is retained and confidential to the extent permitted by law.

sections.heading: 3. Risk-Management Framework and Acceptable Use

questions.prompt: Which risk-management framework is adopted (for example, NIST AI RMF 1.0)?

sections.body: {org_name} adopts {rmf_standard} as its AI risk-management framework and maintains an AI acceptable-use policy that governs which AI uses are permitted, restricted, or prohibited.

sections.heading: 4. Recognized-Standard Adoption (Safe-Harbor Posture)

questions.prompt: Who formally approved adoption of the recognized standard, and when?

sections.body: {org_name} has formally adopted the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (or a comparable recognized standard), approved by {adoption_authority}, and operates its AI governance under it. Operation is evidenced by a completed governance assessment mapped to the standard, establishing the safe-harbor posture that TRAIGA rewards.

sections.heading: 5. Continuous Evaluation Cadence

questions.prompt: On what cadence are deployed AI systems re-evaluated (for example, quarterly, or on each material change)?

sections.body: {org_name} re-evaluates its deployed AI systems on a cadence of {eval_cadence}, and documents the improvements made as a result. This satisfies the SB 1964 expectation of a defined evaluation frequency with documented improvement.
